content.text: The excerpt contains multiple nineteenth-century tales and essays. In “How John Pollexfen Made His Fortune,” Lucile Marmont travels to Pollexfen’s gallery, where he removes her eye for photographic research; her lover Courtland later visits Pollexfen’s den, sacrifices his own eye, and marries her. “The Aztec Princess” follows an antiquities enthusiast from New York to Nicaragua, Palenque, Casa Grande, and a hidden living Aztec city, where Pio teaches him hieroglyphics. Other pieces recount haunted Lake Bigler, mermaids, a telescopic-eyed boy in San Francisco, volcanic catastrophe at Dudzeele, moral and patriotic poems, Washington’s contrast with George III, the Summerfield murder, scientific progress, liberty, marriage, and spiritual evolution.
